pr.title: Separate How projects work from the project list
pr.head: 20b92ec89bdee3038869c5f9a7ff91ad99002516

summary: A repository's Projector site has a Projects page that lists every plan in one table per status, such as in-progress and completed. Below the tables, the page shows a collapsible How projects work introduction, rendered from docs/projects/README.md.

That introduction sat only 4px below the last table, so it read as a stray line attached to the final status group rather than a section of its own. The 4px top margin made sense when the introduction sat under the filter box. Pull request #250 moved the introduction to the bottom of the page and did not change the margin.

This pull request raises the introduction's top margin to 32px. That is more than the 24px gap between one status group and the next, so the introduction reads as separate from the list. Nothing else changes: no markup, no TypeScript, and no colors.

groups.title: Space above the introduction
groups.kicker: One margin in the site stylesheet
intro: The Projects page's script, showProjects in site/src/site.ts, draws the status tables and then appends a <details class="pintro"> element for the introduction. The .pintro rule in site/assets/site.css sets that element's margins, and this group changes only its top margin.

files.note: The site's shared stylesheet. The .pintro top margin goes from 4px to 32px.

checks.text: Only the Projects page uses the pintro class. A search of the head finds it in showProjects, its compiled copy in site.js, a test, and the four .pintro rules, and nowhere in the summary pages' summary.css or summary.js.

The full 32px shows on the page. The last status table ends with no bottom margin, because neither .tblwrap nor table.tbl sets one, so nothing collapses into the gap. Each status heading, .pgroup h2, has a 24px top margin, so the introduction sits further from the list than one group sits from the next.
No media query overrides .pintro, so the margin is the same at narrow widths. The rule sets no color, so the light and dark themes are unaffected.
